title: Krachtorte (Crack Torte)
description: A cake made with almonds, almond oil, and cream.
steps: Blanch 1 pound almonds, peel them, cut them finely and lengthwise, and roast them with 1 pound refined sugar in a brass pan under constant stirring until the sugar becomes yellow
Brush a melon mold with almond oil
Press the seams well with some of the roasted almonds
Warm the rest and fill the mold completely with them
When the torte has cooled, turn it upright onto a plate so that the opening faces upward
Whip 1 schoppen cream in a bowl with a stiff whisk until it resembles egg snow
Let it drain a little on a hair sieve and mix in 3 loth vanilla sugar

title: Krebsdampfnudeln (Crayfish Steamed Noodles)
description: Prepared with crayfish, beer, and cream.

Beat it for a quarter hour, set it in warmth and let it rise

For the sauce: cook together 1/2 maas of milk, zest of 1 lemon, 1 piece of whole cinnamon, and 2 loth of sugar
Beat 3 egg yolks in a pot and stir smooth with 3 finger-widths of flour and cold milk
Gradually pour the boiling milk to it and let everything boil together once more

Take out the gall from the top of the body

Steam the pounded mixture in a casserole until it foams
Pour water on it and cook for a quarter hour
Pour the butter onto cold water and when firm, beat it foamy in a bowl
Grate 2 pieces of bread at the grater, soak in milk, press out firmly, and add to the butter
Add salt and nutmeg flower
Mince the tails and claws finely, add to the mass, and bind with 3 eggs

title: Krebspudding (Crayfish Pudding)
description: A pudding made with crayfish, water or meat or broth, and rolls.
steps: Remove the gall and tails from 25 crayfish

Steam the pounded mixture with 1/4 pound butter in a casserole until it foams

Pour it into cold water and stir until white in a bowl
Take half the crayfish butter and mix with 2 soaked and pressed rolls, 5 egg yolks, 1 grated nutmeg, salt and the snow from 5 egg whites
Place the crayfish tails on a wet cloth
Fill the mass on top
Bind the cloth and cook the pudding in boiling water for one hour

Turn it several times in the butter
Rinse with water and fill with meat broth
Add some crayfish broth, 1 knife tip of nutmeg flower, salt and 1 spoonful sour cream

title: Königin von Brasilien (Queen of Brazil)
description: Prepared with cream, yeast, and chocolate.
steps: Prepare a fine Gugelhopf or Munich butter loaf the day before.
Beat 1/2 pound butter in a bowl for half an hour until foamy.
Place 10 eggs in warm water and stir into the butter one by one (each egg must be stirred for 3 minutes).
Stir in 1/2 schoppen thick, sweet, warm cream, a knife-tip of salt, and 1 loth sugar for another quarter hour.
Stir in 10 tablespoons fine flour until no flour is visible, then 3 tablespoons good white yeast.
Grease a tall vessel with butter, fill with the batter, place in gentle warmth, let it rise until it begins to sink again, and bake in gentle heat until golden.
Stand the baked loaf upright on a plate and when ready to serve, carefully cut off the lid level with the top.
Remove the interior with a spoon so no hole remains.
Dissolve 3/4 pound chocolate in a brass pan with 1 schoppen water.

Beat 24 egg yolks in a pot, heat the chocolate with 1 maas milk until boiling, pour onto the egg yolks, add 1 cooking spoon flour, cook again in the pan with constant stirring, pour through a hair sieve into another vessel, and let cool slightly.
Fill the cream into the hollowed Munich loaf and carefully replace the lid.
Place on a large round plate.

Beat the snow from 24 egg whites and cover the bread and plate up to the middle band with it, making the mixture as high as possible with a rough, mountain-like appearance, creating a cross-cut at the top to give it a crown shape.
Dissolve 3/4 pound chocolate again in a brass pan with 1 glass water, add 1/2 pound sugar, add 1 more glass water, and cook everything together for a quarter hour.
Brush the chocolate glaze over a brush onto the snow mountain until completely covered.
Place a beautiful cherry at each of the 4 corners of the crown and a beautiful apricot in the middle.
Before the snow goes onto the torte, place it in the oven for a quarter hour to warm it again, but not after.

title: Königsragout (Royal Ragout)
description: Prepared with shallot, bread, and lemon juice.
steps: Grind leftover calf roast very finely with lemon zest and marrow.
Add 6 diced, braised shallot onions and a soaked, wrung-out bread roll.
Lightly cream quarter pound butter, add the ground meat mixture, and stir in 4 eggs, salt, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Butter a suitable baking dish, pour in the mixture, make a hollow in the center, and bake in the oven until golden.

Make a mushroom sauce: brown one spoonful of flour in butter, deglaze with cold water, add one glass red Burgundy and half a ladleful of good stock, and cook the ox palates in this sauce.
Add 6 to 8 mushroom pieces, 4 to 5 cleaned, peeled, and sliced truffles, salt, nutmeg, pepper, mace, and lemon juice and zest.
Cut the breasts from 2 young chickens, place in lukewarm water until white, clean 2 sweetbreads, lard both beautifully, and braise in butter with half a sliced lemon for a quarter hour.
Add them to the ox palates with the braising fat.
Make a dumpling batter from cleaned morels, crushed truffles, quarter pound pork forcemeat, a small handful of bread, and an egg white; form small dumplings the size of hazelnuts and fry in lard.
Add to the ragout.
Place the baked cake on a platter, pour the ragout into the hollow, lay the chicken breasts and mushrooms on top, garnish with lemon, and pour melted consommé over the chicken breasts.

title: Pike Ragout (Fish Ragout)
description: Prepared with pike, onions, and lemons.

ingredients.name: 2 to 3 half- or three-quarter-pound pike, cleaned and prepared

steps: Cut the cleaned pike into finger-width pieces and rub them well with salt and pepper
Place a piece of butter in a casserole with the fish, some onions and lemons, cover and let steam for half an hour
Prepare the calf's thymus by removing the throat, blanch it briefly, cut into pieces and add to the fish
From 8 large cooked crayfish, remove the tails and claws, clean the bodies carefully so the upper shell remains whole
Pound the remaining crayfish bodies with 1/4 pound butter together, place in a casserole, steam until it foams, then strain through a sieve so the butter runs off well

Stir in 2 eggs one after another
Remove the long beard and claw from the crayfish shells, fill the shells with the mixture and place them upside down in a dish

Sprinkle 3 finger widths of flour strongly over the fish, pour on 1/2 glass wine and some meat broth, add the crayfish tails and claws
Arrange on a plate and lay the crayfish shells and ragout on top

title: Preisselbeeren (Lingonberries)

steps: Prepare the berries as for compote.

description: Prepared with fat and water.
steps: Cut the beef fat into small cubes and soak in water for a day or night so any blood particles can be removed

title: Rinderschmorbraten (Braised Beef Roast for 6 Persons)
description: Prepared with beef, bacon, and bread.
steps: The meat is beaten and tied with twine into good shape. The bacon is cut into 4 cm long, 8 mm thick strips and turned in the crushed spice mixed with salt. With a pointed wooden stick, the bacon strips are inserted into the meat piece at equal distances and this is then turned in flour mixed with a little salt.

In the meantime, fat—also bacon scraps—is made hot and brown in an earthenware pot, the meat is browned on all sides, using a skimming spoon and a ladle for turning, then onions, crumbled bread crust and the remaining spice are added, gradually 1/4 l hot water is poured on, the pot is tightly covered, weighted with a bolt and the meat is slowly braised at the side of the fire. Every half hour it is turned to another side and the reduced sauce is replenished with hot water. For this replenishment, one can add beer or, if the piece lay in a vinegar marinade, some of it as desired. After 3 hours, the soft braised piece is removed from the pot, covered with a deep bowl, the sauce is degreased and checked for its binding, according to which it is either thinned with any liquids or thickened with a little cornstarch, mixed cold.
